title: Two clues in one life
hook: One animal can challenge a familiar category rule.

knows: Animals have body structures and life histories.
doesNotKnow: Distinguish an egg-laying mammal from a bird.

misconception: A familiar animal feature always has the first explanation that comes to mind.
objective: Distinguish an egg-laying mammal from a bird.

claims.text: An echidna lays eggs and feeds its young milk. Which conclusion follows? The diagram pairs an egg with milk feeding in the same life history. Echidnas are monotremes: mammals that lay eggs. Laying an egg alone does not rule out membership in the mammal group.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, mammals and monotremes, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The diagram and its labels are schematic, not to scale and not an observation. One life history · schematic
A platypus lays eggs and feeds its young milk. Can it be a mammal? Monotremes are egg-laying mammals; feeding young milk is a mammalian trait.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, mammals and monotremes, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

recall.question: A platypus lays eggs and feeds its young milk. Can it be a mammal?
recall.why: Monotremes are egg-laying mammals; feeding young milk is a mammalian trait.
